newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB-Ukraine '97 winter grain output seen up.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-Ukraine '97 winter grain output seen up.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from the Agrokhleb Report, published by SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.
MOSCOW, Dec 9 - In Ukraine, favourable conditions for winter grain sowing normally last up until the end of September.
This year, grain producers failed to sow all their winter grains during this period, mainly due to fuel shortages.
By September 30, they had sown only 68 percent of the target. However, unusually warm weather favoured winter grain sowing in October and even into November.
As a result, the total area planted to winter grains has reached 7.4 million hectares, including 6.5 million ha of winter wheat, 0.5 million hectare of rye and 0.4 million ha of barley.
In most regions, winter grain plantings are in good condition and soil moisture is adequate for growth.

Assuming average winter conditions, winter wheat output (which accounts for the bulk of the country's total wheat production) may rise to 17 million tonnes next year from 13.7 million tonnes in 1996. Total winter grain output is tentatively forecast at 20 million tonnes, some 3.5 million tonnes above 1996 output. -- Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
